title: Rav Huna Zuta
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Beitzah 29b](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.29b.4): Rava bar Rav Huna Zuta; Dikdukei Soferim reads Rabbah, and so it is in [Ketubot 69a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.69a.14), Rabbah bar Rav Huna Zuta. Hyman infers from Beitzah that the Rava/Rabbah mentioned is the son of Rav Huna without further designation, agreeing with Yuchasin, since Rav Huna was a short man.[^2]

notes.text: The inference identifies the father called Huna Zuta with Rav Huna without further designation; it does not turn the entry’s Huna into his own son. The William Davidson digital Beitzah 29b has Rava bar Rav Huna Zutei and Ketubot 69a has Rabbah bar Rav Huna Zuta; the identification and short-stature argument remain Hyman’s.

The linked Beitzah text reads Rava and has him teaching at Neharde’a; Ketubot reads Rabbah and has him receive a letter there. Heilprin considers whether the two name forms refer to one figure in his [entry on Rabbah](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3140&lang=en) and discusses the epithet and the father in his [entry on Rav Huna Zuta](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=959&lang=en). The Dikdukei Soferim and Yuchasin readings above are Hyman’s reports.
